name: WorkMeetingQuarterlyPlanning_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Quarterly planning meeting. Felix, Amara, Derek, Brendan, Aaliya. Hybrid. Competing priorities across engineering, product, sales, marketing, HR. Everyone making a case. Sigma asked for a date or capacity figure.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, hybrid video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a quarterly planning meeting. Felix protects engineering capacity. Amara defends the product roadmap. Derek has pipeline commitments. Brendan has a campaign needing engineering support. Aaliya raises a team health concern that affects capacity. Sigma is consulted for a figure or deadline.

setting.mood: Professional negotiation. Everyone advocating. Nobody being unreasonable.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Cross-functional peers. Mutual respect with tension over resources.
setting.background: Q-planning happens every three months. Never enough engineering capacity.
setting.conversation_style: Each person makes a case. Overlapping priorities. Aaliya raises the people angle.

scenario_template.topic: Amara, Derek and Brendan lay out their Q priorities.
Aaliya flags a team health concern affecting one engineer's availability.
scenario_template.note: Felix knew, others didn't. Amara recalibrates.

scenario_template.topic: Felix or Derek asks Sigma for a capacity figure or deadline.
scenario_template.note: The figure makes the constraint concrete. No assistant present.

scenario_template.topic: Group negotiates prioritisation. Trade-offs made explicitly.
scenario_template.note: Derek gets his timeline. Brendan gets partial. Amara protects core product work.

scenario_template.topic: Committed Q priorities. Some things explicitly deferred.
scenario_template.note: Felix states what engineering can commit to.

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: Engineering manager protecting capacity. Has a people situation others didn't know about.

user2.name: Amara
user2.role: PM defending the product roadmap. Evidence-based and diplomatic.

user3.name: Derek
user3.role: VP Sales. Needs the pipeline commitment met.

user4.name: Brendan
user4.role: Marketing. Campaign needs engineering. Has a business case.

user5.name: Aaliya
user5.role: HR BP. Flags the people concern. Has context others don't.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: Sigma answers meeting questions in one or two sentences maximum
Accidental triggers should come from plausible meeting language
After an accidental trigger the speaker says 'not you, Sigma' or similar and continues
Sigma does not proactively participate — only responds when addressed
